question: What makes an injection truly safe in healthcare?

options.A: It causes no harm to the patient or healthcare worker
options.B: It costs less than oral medications
options.C: It is performed only by senior doctors
options.D: It is always administered in the gluteal muscle

explanation: Spot on! A safe injection protects everyone—the patient getting treated, you as the healthcare worker, and our community from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why should nurses care about why patients stay silent when safety rules are skipped?

options.A: It reduces the need to sterilize reusable equipment
options.B: Patients are usually at fault for bad clinical outcomes
options.C: It proves that hospitals have enough medical supplies
options.D: Understanding patient silence helps nurses improve safety advocacy

explanation: You got it! When we understand why patients keep quiet, we can break those barriers and speak up better for their safety. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do many patients view healthcare workers when it comes to authority?

options.A: As temporary service providers who must follow orders
options.B: As individuals who frequently make intentional errors
options.C: As peers with identical medical training
options.D: As absolute authority figures whose judgment is unquestionable

explanation: Exactly! Culturally, many patients see healthcare providers as infallible experts, which makes them hesitant to speak up or ask questions. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h2)

question: A patient sees a nurse open a pre-used syringe pack but says nothing. What is the main reason for this silence?

options.A: A desire to test the nurse's clinical skills
options.C: A preference for receiving injections over tablets
options.D: Power imbalance and fear of appearing disrespectful

explanation: Spot on! Patients often swallow their worries because they are scared of offending someone they view as superior. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which dangerous infections can spread when unsterile syringes are reused?
explanation: Correct! Reusing syringes is a major way bloodborne infections like HIV and hepatitis spread globally. Safety first, always! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why does a lack of health awareness stop patients from insisting on safe injections?

options.A: They have enough money to buy private syringes
options.B: They prefer taking bitter oral medications instead
options.C: They understand hospital sterilization protocols fully
options.D: They do not know what hazards to look out for

explanation: You nailed it. If a patient doesn't know the risks, they won't know what dangerous practices to watch out for or what to demand. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is a very common local belief about injected medications compared to pills?

options.A: Pills are absorbed directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Pills are always more expensive than injections
options.C: Injections have zero risk of side effects
options.D: Injections are believed to work faster and more powerfully

explanation: That's right! Many people hold the myth that injections are stronger magic because they go straight into the body. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h4)

question: How does a patient's desperate desire to recover quickly affect their injection choices?

options.A: It causes them to demand extra laboratory testing first
options.B: It drives them to refuse all forms of parenteral therapy
options.C: It makes them prioritize fast relief over questioning safety practices
options.D: It encourages them to thoroughly inspect every single medical package

explanation: Spot on! When someone just wants to get well and get back to their daily hustle, safety checks take a back seat. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is a major fear that stops patients from questioning healthcare providers?

options.A: Fear of paying extra taxes for medical equipment
options.B: Fear of being discharged without a diagnosis
options.C: Fear of retaliation or being neglected by staff
options.D: Fear that the medicine will expire too quickly

explanation: Correct! Patients often worry that if they complain or ask too many questions, the staff might treat them poorly or ignore them. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why do patients in areas with few clinics feel extra pressured to stay quiet?

options.A: They receive free private insurance coverage
options.C: They have few alternative clinics to go to if they are mistreated
options.D: They are legally forbidden from speaking to nurses

explanation: You got it! When there's nowhere else to go for care, patients feel too dependent to risk upsetting the staff. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: What resource problem often leads to unsafe injection practices in underfunded clinics?

options.B: Severe shortages of sterile needles and syringes
options.C: An excess of trained supervisory personnel

explanation: Spot on. When a facility runs out of basic gear, stressed workers are put in tough spots where maintaining safety becomes a struggle. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: How do rushed staff and chaotic hospital environments affect patients?

options.B: Patients feel intimidated and hesitate to question busy workers
options.C: Patients feel inspired to volunteer and help prepare medications
options.D: Patients report the hospital to international boards immediately

explanation: Correct! When a ward is super busy and chaotic, patients feel it's rude or risky to slow things down with questions. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a simple thing a nurse can do to build trust about injection safety?

options.A: Ask the doctor to perform all medication preparations
options.B: Show the sterile needle pack to the patient before opening it
options.C: Administer all injections behind a closed privacy curtain
options.D: Hide the syringe until the procedure is completely finished

explanation: Wonderful! Showing an unopened, sterile pack instantly reassures the patient that you take their safety seriously. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h7)

question: How can a nurse best encourage patients to speak up about safety concerns?

options.A: Only discuss safety protocols with senior medical doctors
options.B: Invite questions and explain procedures in simple, friendly terms
options.C: Warn patients never to question clinical staff decisions
options.D: Leave all safety education brochures on an unmonitored desk

explanation: You nailed it! Welcoming questions and keeping your explanations warm and simple helps chase away patient fears. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h7)
